- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising prices) with low sentiment, it overestimates upside — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model tends to lag behind true price — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for delayed reaction.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive declines after peak), model often fails to recognize — reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates volatility — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% in early days if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
